findings.description: `_effort_on_wire` now unconditionally calls `cls.wire_effort(...)` for any adapter class returned by `adapter_class_for_type`. The prior implementation only handled CLI passthrough and Anthropic HTTP; other providers returned `None`. Unless every registered adapter class implements `wire_effort`, invoking a non-Anthropic provider with an effort value will raise `AttributeError` while emitting MODELINV completion telemetry.
findings.failure_mode: A request whose resolved hop has `effort` set but whose adapter class lacks `wire_effort` crashes during audit emission/result finalization instead of completing successfully.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the hook lookup, e.g. `wire_effort = getattr(cls, "wire_effort", None); return wire_effort(...) if callable(wire_effort) else None`, or add a default `wire_effort` classmethod to the adapter base class and ensure all registered adapters inherit it.

findings.description: In the `except ChevalError` branch, a hop whose error carries `failure_class: opt_in_required` is appended to `_models_not_planned`, but that hop is still present in `_modelinv_models_requested` (the agy-alone chain is deliberately left whole by `_plan_around_agy`) and it WAS dispatched (adapter.complete() ran and refused). The new `models_not_planned` parameter in `audit/modelinv.py:emit_model_invoke_complete` is documented as 'hops cheval did not plan (never dispatched)', and the test module docstring states a not-planned hop 'is not in models_requested'. The refusal path violates both: the same canonical appears in `models_requested` and `models_not_planned`, with `models_failed` empty.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV records for an INVALID_CONFIG refusal show voices_planned=1, succeeded=0, failed=0, not_planned=[same hop]. Any verdict-quality or audit consumer that derives planned voices from `models_requested` and health from `models_failed` sees a planned voice that neither failed nor succeeded, and can label the record ok/APPROVED while the process exited INVALID_CONFIG. Double-membership also breaks any consumer that treats the two lists as disjoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the refused hop from `_modelinv_state['models_requested']` when recording it as not planned (so the two lists stay disjoint and the 'never dispatched' doc holds), or keep it in `models_failed` with `error_class: INVALID_CONFIG` and a distinct reason such as `refused_opt_in`, and update the modelinv.py docstring/schema enum accordingly.

findings.description: The reduced chain is rebuilt via `_RC(primary_alias=..., entries=kept, headless_mode=..., headless_mode_source=...)`, enumerating four fields by hand. Any other field on `ResolvedChain` (now or added later: capability/thinking class, ceiling policy, exhaustion reason, source metadata) is silently reset to its default on the re-planned chain only, with no test coverage because the test config exercises just these four.
findings.failure_mode: A future or existing optional field on ResolvedChain is dropped only when an agy hop was planned around, producing behaviour that differs between opt-in-on and opt-in-off runs of the same chain and is hard to trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `dataclasses.replace(chain, entries=kept)` (or an equivalent copy-with-entries helper on ResolvedChain) so every other field is carried over verbatim.

findings.description: The new loop validates `extra.reasoning_effort` against EFFORT_LEVELS (low|medium|high|xhigh|max) and emits a once-per-process WARN saying the value is 'ignored' when it does not match. `reasoning_effort` is the codex/grok adapters' own key and codex legitimately accepts `minimal`, which is not in EFFORT_LEVELS. For such an entry cheval now logs a misleading WARN, resolve_effort returns (None, 'none'), `_effort_on_wire` short-circuits on `effort is None`, so MODELINV records effort=None/effort_effective=None while the codex adapter still puts `minimal` on the wire from its own extra.
findings.failure_mode: Spurious config-smell WARN on a valid catalog entry, and MODELINV effort telemetry that contradicts what the adapter actually sent.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `reasoning_effort` against the owning adapter's accepted set (or only against the cheval set when the adapter is claude-headless), or extend the accepted values for that key; at minimum do not say 'ignored' for a key the adapter reads independently.

findings.description: `_plan_around_agy` is applied late, immediately before the MODELINV state is built, and the diff re-derives only `_auth_type_resolved` from the new primary. Under `prefer-cli` with the opt-in off, the original chain's primary is the agy hop; any other value derived from `_chain.entries[0]` before this point (effort resolution for the primary, dry-run output of the resolved model/chain, provider-config/adapter selection for the primary) was computed against a hop that will never be dispatched.
findings.failure_mode: `--dry-run` or pre-walk telemetry can report the agy hop as the resolved primary while the real walk dispatches the API hop, and primary-derived settings may reflect the wrong entry. Only the auth type is corrected.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the `_plan_around_agy` call to directly after chain resolution so every downstream consumer of `_chain` (dry-run, effort, auth type, adapter selection, MODELINV) sees the planned chain, and drop the special-case re-derivation of `_auth_type_resolved`.

findings.description: The new `.claude/adapters/cheval.py` is test code placed at the production module/script path. It imports `cheval` from inside `cheval.py`, so normal `import cheval` resolves to this partially initialized test module rather than a real implementation with `cmd_invoke`, `EXIT_CODES`, etc.
findings.failure_mode: Any production caller or CLI entrypoint that imports or executes `.claude/adapters/cheval.py` will fail at runtime with missing attributes or recursive/self-import behavior instead of invoking the adapter command.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these tests under the test tree, for example `.claude/adapters/tests/test_cheval_agy_chain.py`, and leave `.claude/adapters/cheval.py` as the production implementation.

findings.description: The hunk writes a pytest module into `.claude/adapters/cheval.py`, which is the CLI entry point the rest of the change set depends on (the same module the tests call as `cheval.cmd_invoke`, `cheval.EXIT_CODES`, `cheval._load_persona`, `cheval.load_config`, and that `resolve_effort` / `_effort_on_wire` live in per the reviewer context). The content is unmistakably a test file: `import pytest`, `import cheval`, nine `test_*` functions, and path arithmetic that is only correct for a file under `.claude/adapters/tests/` (`sys.path.insert(0, Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)` must yield `.claude/adapters` for `import cheval` and `from loa_cheval.types import ...` to resolve; `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]` must yield the repo root for the schema path). Placed at `.claude/adapters/cheval.py`, `parent.parent` is `.claude/` and `parents[3]` is the directory above the repo. The hunk header `-0,0` shows no removed lines against a non-empty prior blob (`ca85d389`), so the previous 232-line-plus body of cheval.py is unaccounted for. Additionally, the production change this hunk's tests exercise — the chain walk that records `models_not_planned`, the `_AGY_NOT_PLANNED_WARNED` once-flag, the `failure_class` field in the JSON error envelope, the `modelinv.py` emitter, `loader.routes_to_agy` / `warn_agy_available_once` / `_AGY_TYPE_WARNED` / `_AGY_AVAILABLE_WARNED`, the retry breaker exemption, and the `AgyOptInRequiredError` constructor change — appears nowhere in the diff, so the schema property added in this change set has no producer within it.
findings.failure_mode: If applied as shown: every `cheval invoke` (and every consumer that shells out to it — the four bash planners, Flatline, the dissent, Bridgebuilder, `/loa` Providers) loses `main`/`cmd_invoke`; executing the script performs a self-import, defines test functions, and exits with no CLI. The new test module itself fails at collection/runtime with `AttributeError: module 'cheval' has no attribute 'cmd_invoke'` (and `_load_persona`, `EXIT_CODES`), and `test_the_modelinv_schema_declares_models_not_planned` raises `FileNotFoundError` because `parents[3]` escapes the repo. If instead the path header is a mislabel, the diff ships tests and a schema for a `cmd_invoke` behaviour change that is not in the diff, so the G1/G5 guarantee (gated agy hop never dispatched, `failure_class: opt_in_required` on the envelope) cannot be verified from this change set.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the module as `.claude/adapters/tests/test_cheval_agy_chain_walk.py` (new file, `index 0000000..`), restore `.claude/adapters/cheval.py` to its real content, and include the production hunks the tests depend on (`cheval.py` cmd_invoke chain-walk planning + `_AGY_NOT_PLANNED_WARNED` + envelope `failure_class`; `loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py` `models_not_planned`; `loa_cheval/config/loader.py` `routes_to_agy`, `warn_agy_available_once`, `_AGY_TYPE_WARNED`, `_AGY_AVAILABLE_WARNED`; `loa_cheval/providers/retry.py` breaker exemption; `loa_cheval/types.py` `AgyOptInRequiredError`; `agy_headless_adapter.py` `validate_config`) in the same change set so the schema and tests are reviewable against their producer.

findings.description: G1 states a gated agy hop is "never dispatched" and the MODELINV record says `models_not_planned` / not in `models_requested`. For the two agy-alone cases (`test_direct_gemini_headless_still_refuses_with_failure_class` and `test_cli_only_google_voice_is_agy_alone_and_refuses`) the tests inject `dispatch=_refuse` that raises `AgyOptInRequiredError` and never assert on `seen`. They therefore pass both if cheval refuses pre-dispatch with an empty planned chain and if cheval dispatches the sole hop and relies on the adapter's own gate to refuse. In the second case the emitted MODELINV says the hop was not planned and `models_requested` is empty while a dispatch did occur, and cheval's own planning gate (the point of this round) is not actually what prevents the argv-exposure path — the adapter gate is. The supplied `_refuse` stub suggests the author expected a dispatch to happen.
findings.failure_mode: A regression that makes cheval dispatch a gated agy-alone hop (e.g. a mode branch that forgets to filter) is not caught by these tests; telemetry then under-reports a dispatch that happened, and the G1 'never dispatched' claim rests solely on the adapter-level gate.
findings.suggested_fix: In both tests assert `seen == []` and `payload.get("models_requested", []) == []`; drop the `dispatch=_refuse` stub so a stray dispatch surfaces as a success rather than the expected INVALID_CONFIG. If cheval currently does dispatch the sole hop, change `cmd_invoke` to raise `AgyOptInRequiredError` itself when the planned chain is empty after filtering.

findings.description: The header comment added at the soft-source site says the planner 'fails closed (every hop agy-checked) if the lib did not load', but _adv_agy_filter_chain does the opposite: when _adv_agy_lib returns false it logs a WARN and returns the chain unfiltered, so a gemini-headless hop stays planned. Before this diff the inline reader filtered the literal gemini-headless hop with no library dependency, so a consumer checkout where .claude/scripts/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh is missing or stale (the soft `source ... 2>/dev/null || true` exists precisely to tolerate that) now regresses from 'planned: false, reason: opt_in_required' to 'planned, then refused/skipped by cheval'. Additionally, agy_gate_warn_once is invoked inside _adv_agy_filter_chain, which main calls under $(...), against the lib's own contract that the once-flag is a shell variable and must not be set from a subshell; it is only quiet today because main calls it at top level first.
findings.failure_mode: With the lib absent, the companion chain keeps the agy hop; the dissent envelope records that voice as a cheval refusal/skip instead of opt_in_required, and the top-of-file comment misleads the next maintainer into assuming fail-closed planning.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a minimal inline fallback in _adv_agy_filter_chain for the lib-missing path (drop hops whose raw or canonical id matches gemini-headless|*:gemini-headless|gemini-headless:*), and correct the header comment. Remove the agy_gate_warn_once call from inside _adv_agy_filter_chain and rely on the top-level call in main.

findings.description: The flavor fallback is selected by output shape, not by yq flavor: if the typed go-yq expression yields anything other than the literal 'true'/'false', the function re-runs `yq '.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in == true'`. That untyped comparison is only a typed test under python yq (jq semantics). Under mikefarah go yq, `==` on two scalars compares node values as strings, so a quoted string "true" compares equal to boolean true. Today go yq cannot realistically reach the fallback (the first expression always prints true/false for any node), so there is no live exposure, but the library's single stated invariant — a string "true" never opts in — now rests on an incidental property of the first expression rather than on the branch guard.
findings.failure_mode: If a future go-yq version changes the output of the tag-test expression (e.g. multi-line or styled output), the fallback runs under go yq and `agy_opt_in: "true"` silently opts the planner into the agy route, defeating the gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Select the fallback by detecting the python flavor explicitly (e.g. `yq --version 2>&1 | grep -qi jq` or the absence of 'mikefarah'/'v4'), or restrict the fallback to only run when the first call exited non-zero AND the flavor is python. Alternatively make the python branch typed too: `(.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in | type) == "boolean" and .hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in == true`.

findings.cross_file_justification: routes_to_agy is introduced in the diff and is consumed by run-preflight.sh P3 (also diff-touched: the source line). P3 uses the predicate only on the gated branch; with the opt-in on it falls through to a usability check that does not know the voice is agy-routed.
findings.description: P3 calls routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode" only when p3_agy_on is 0. When the opt-in is true and mode is cli-only, a Google API model such as gemini-2.5-pro (or google:gemini-*) is agy-routed per the shared predicate, but cli_for returns "" for it, so usability is decided by cred_present google (GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY) rather than by `agy` being on PATH. P3 can therefore report PASS for a stage whose only voice cannot run on this host, and STAGE_ONLY/P4 will attribute it to the google provider's API breaker rather than the headless one.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight passes, the run starts, and the stage's voice fails at dispatch with PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE (agy binary absent) — the exact 'planned voice that cannot exist' G-1 is meant to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: After computing cli, add: `if routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode"; then cli=agy; fi` so the agy-routed voice is judged by `command -v agy` like the other *-headless hops, and label it `(cli agy)` in usable_names/missing.

findings.description: When agy opt-in is enabled, Google models that `routes_to_agy` under `cli-only` are no longer treated as CLI-routed for availability. The new gate only skips them when opt-in is off, but the later usability check still uses `cli_for`, which returns `agy` only for `gemini-headless`, not for routed Google model IDs like `gemini-2.5-pro`. That means a Google API credential can make a cli-only agy-routed voice look usable even when `agy` is not on PATH.
findings.failure_mode: The P3/adversarial review availability check can PASS with a Google credential but no agy CLI, then the actual planned headless route cannot run. This violates the shared routing rule introduced by the diff and can leave a configured review stage with no executable voice despite the preflight reporting one.
findings.suggested_fix: After computing `routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode"`, use that routed result to force `cli=agy` for availability when opt-in is on, or add a shared helper that returns the effective transport/CLI for a model under the selected headless mode and use it for both gating and usability.

findings.description: The hunk introduces p3_mode (agy_headless_mode) and the shared routes_to_agy predicate, but consults them only to decide the gated-off case `(( ! p3_agy_on )) && routes_to_agy`. Once the opt-in is on, the usable-voice decision falls through to the pre-existing mode-blind pair: `cli=$(cli_for "$m")` (non-empty only for literal *-headless names) and otherwise `cred_present "$prov"`. Under `hounfour.headless.mode: cli-only` a Google voice such as `gemini-2.5-pro` or `google:gemini-3.1-pro` (rows the new conformance table marks routes_to_agy=True) therefore gets cli="" and is judged usable by a GOOGLE/GEMINI key, although the shared rule — the one this diff exists to adopt — says that voice dispatches through the `agy` binary and never touches the key. The same mismatch exists for the `gemini-headless:any` form: routes_to_agy returns True but the rewritten cli_for strips only a leading provider prefix and returns "" for a trailing `:suffix`, so with the opt-in on it is checked as a credential voice. (Context: the diff header labels this file adversarial-review.sh, but the hunk is the run-preflight P3 block; the P3 result also feeds STAGE_ONLY/P4 via `provs`.)
findings.failure_mode: cli-only + opt-in true + Gemini key set + no `agy` on PATH: P3 reports `code_review usable: gemini-2.5-pro` and PASSes; the review/Flatline run then starts and the voice fails at dispatch (PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE), i.e. a planned voice that cannot exist — the G-1 outcome the sprint is meant to make impossible. Inverse: cli-only + opt-in true + `agy` installed + no key → P3 marks the voice `missing` and FAILs a stage that would actually run.
findings.suggested_fix: After the gate, derive the resource from the same predicate instead of cli_for alone: e.g. `if routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode"; then cli=agy; fi` (or make cli_for take the mode and delegate to agy-gate-lib), so the `command -v agy` branch is taken for every agy-routed voice and usable_names shows `(cli agy)`. Also normalise a trailing `:suffix` in cli_for (or reuse the lib's model-id normaliser) so `gemini-headless:any` maps to agy. Add a run-preflight.bats case: cli-only, opt-in true, key present, agy absent → FAIL/missing `(cli agy)`.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/agy-gate-conformance.bats:AGC-7 (case "$w" in bool) branch) and AGC-1 (`! agy_opted_in "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.yaml"`)
findings.description: Two of the new conformance assertions are vacuous under bats/`set -e` semantics. In AGC-7 the boolean branch is `bool) [ "$output" = on ] && [ "$py" = on ] ;;` — a bare `&&` list. If the bash lib returns `off` for a boolean true, the first test fails, the list short-circuits, and because the failing command precedes `&&` neither `set -e` nor the ERR trap fires; the loop simply continues. Only the Python half (the final command of the list) can fail the test. In AGC-1, `! agy_opted_in "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.yaml"` is a mid-test negation; bash exempts `!`-prefixed pipelines from `set -e`, so a lib that returned 0 on a missing file would pass unnoticed. Elsewhere the file correctly uses the `! cmd || { ...; return 1; }` idiom, so these two are inconsistencies rather than a pattern.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in agy_opted_in (boolean true → off in bash, or success on a missing config) is not caught by the suite that the SDD D-1.5/G12 rulings cite as the parity evidence; the report's 'every reader says so' claim rests partly on checks that cannot fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same guarded idiom as the rest of the file: `bool) [ "$output" = on ] && [ "$py" = on ] || { echo "bool: bash=$output py=$py"; return 1; } ;;` and `run ! agy_opted_in "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.yaml"` (bats ≥1.5, already required) or `! agy_opted_in ... || { echo ...; return 1; }`.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/agy-gate-conformance.bats:AGC-9 (and the loa-status --json `! grep -q 'WARN'` check in AGC-8)
findings.description: AGC-9's environment isolation is inconsistent with its guard. The commands run with `PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname "$(command -v yq)")"`, but the 'nothing available → silent' guard only checks `PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" command -v agy`. On any host where `agy` is installed next to yq (~/.local/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin — the usual case for both tools) the guard passes, the lib sees `agy` on PATH, and `[ -z "$stderr" ]` fails. The second assertion ('a Google/Gemini key is set') is not guarded at all and depends on `agy` being absent from the yq directory; if it is present the WARN reason may read 'agy on PATH' instead. If yq is the Python flavour (the P3 code still branches on YQ_FLAVOUR), its `jq` dependency must also be reachable from the restricted PATH. Separately, AGC-8 asserts `! grep -q 'WARN'` over the entire stderr of `loa-status.sh --json` run against the real repo with empty run/env dirs — any unrelated WARN emitted by loa-status (missing beads, missing CLI, etc.) fails the agy test.
findings.failure_mode: The suite is green on the implementer's host (where `agy` is absent, per the report) but fails or flakes on a host with `agy` installed or with loa-status emitting an unrelated WARN, eroding trust in the conformance suite that is cited as the D-1.5/D-1.7 evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute one restricted PATH variable (`rp="/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname "$(command -v yq)")"`), use it for both the guard (`PATH="$rp" command -v agy`) and the runs, and apply the same guard (or `skip`) to the 'key is set' assertion. In AGC-8 grep for the specific agy WARN texts (`not a YAML boolean`, `agy route is available here`) rather than any `WARN`.

findings.trigger_anchor: tests/unit/agy-gate-conformance.bats:AGC-1 / AGC-7 (the `for v in absent false '"true"' 1 yes` loop vs the `_three` absent|bool|string set)
findings.cross_file_justification: The new conformance suite is the sole evidence that the bash lib and the Python twin agree on the opt-in value. AGC-1 pins bash as *off* for `yes` and `1`, but AGC-7 (the only test that feeds the Python reader) covers just absent / true / "true". yq (go, yaml.v3) resolves `agy_opt_in: yes` to !!str, whereas PyYAML's safe_load (YAML 1.1 schema) resolves yes/no/on/off to a boolean. If loader.py parses with PyYAML and tests `is True`, `agy_opt_in: yes` is ON for cheval and OFF for every bash planner.
findings.description: The parity table has a hole exactly where yq-go and PyYAML are known to disagree. The sprint's stated invariant (SDD D-1.5: ONE predicate; the AC: 'with the opt-in absent or false, cheval refuses … the dissent/Flatline/preflight record not planned') is only pinned on the bash side for YAML 1.1 booleans. An operator who writes `agy_opt_in: yes` (a very common YAML habit) would see `/loa` and run-preflight say 'opt-in (disabled)' while `cheval invoke --model gemini-headless` happily spawns `agy`; or the reverse, a dissent planner filtering a hop that cheval would have dispatched.
findings.failure_mode: Split-brain planning: bash planners mark the voice not planned (no companion runs, P3 FAILs the stage) while cheval, invoked directly or via a chain, treats the route as opted in and spawns `agy` — the unplanned spawn G-1 forbids. Unverified without loader.py in the diff, hence ADVISORY.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AGC-7's `_three` set (or AGC-2's row list) with `yes`, `on`, `1` and `True` fed to both agy_opted_in and agy_opt_in_enabled, and make the Python predicate normalise the raw scalar like yq does (accept only a value the YAML 1.2 core schema tags as !!bool true, e.g. check the node tag with the loader's resolver or compare the raw token against true/True/TRUE) so both sides agree on every row.

findings.description: The new G13 assertion `[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-review.json" ] && [ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-skeptic.json" ]` is a two-operand && list that is followed by further commands in the same @test body. Bash (and therefore bats, which relies on `set -eET` plus an ERR trap) does not fire errexit or the ERR trap for any command in a && list except the one after the final &&. If tertiary-review.json EXISTS, the first test returns 1, the list short-circuits, no trap fires, and the next line (`! grep -q gemini-headless ...`) resets $?. The test passes. Only the tertiary-skeptic.json half of the check can ever fail the test. The comment states the intent is 'no tertiary artefact', so half of that pin is a no-op. (The hunk is labeled .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh in the diff header but the content is the Flatline tertiary opt-in bats suite; see DISS-002.)
findings.failure_mode: If run_phase1 regresses and writes tertiary-review.json for a tertiary that is disabled_by_opt_in (e.g. an empty or error artefact that downstream consensus later reads as a voice), this test stays green. The review-round fix it was added to pin (r251-1 G13) is only verified for the skeptic artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the check a single command or two separate statements so the ERR trap sees each failure, e.g. `[[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-review.json" && ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-skeptic.json" ]]` or two lines: `[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-review.json" ]` then `[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-skeptic.json" ]`. Optionally add an `|| { ls "$TEMP_DIR"; return 1; }` diagnostic like the loop above it. Grep the three touched bats files for other mid-body `] && [` lists.

findings.description: The diff header names `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh` (mode 100755) but both hunks are bats test code: the hunk-context function `_cfg() {  # <tertiary> [agy_opt_in value|absent] [headless mode]`, `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR`, `run --separate-stderr run_phase1 ...`, `run tertiary_opt_in_skip_reason`, `get_model_tertiary`/`get_tertiary_status` assertions and `local f` with `return 1` are the Flatline tertiary opt-in suite (tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats per the sprint report). The pre-existing context lines are already bats syntax, so this is almost certainly a mislabeled path in the diff rather than bats code being inserted into the sourced dissent script. It still needs confirming: if these lines really were applied to adversarial-review.sh, sourcing it would execute test assertions at load time and fail.
findings.failure_mode: If the hunks were genuinely applied to .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh, the dissent script would run bats-only constructs (`run --separate-stderr`, top-level `return 1`, `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]`) when sourced or executed and break every /review dissent invocation. If the path is merely mislabeled, the only consequence is that findings anchored to it (including DISS-001) point at the wrong file.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with `git show --stat` that the hunks landed in tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats and that .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh is unchanged in this commit; regenerate the diff if the header was rewritten by tooling. If the file is genuinely adversarial-review.sh, revert the two hunks and move them to the bats suite.

findings.description: The G15 guard asserts `validateApiKeys.length === 2` and claims this proves 'no default reads the process cwd'. Function.length only drops parameters that carry a default initializer. An optional second parameter (`gate?: AgyGate`) with `gate ?? readAgyGate(loaConfigPathFor(undefined))` inside the body keeps length 2 and reintroduces exactly the cwd read G15 removed. The same describe also pins `loaConfigPathFor(undefined) === ".loa.config.yaml"`, which enshrines a process-cwd fallback as accepted no-root behavior rather than treating a missing repo root as an error.
findings.failure_mode: A later refactor can silently reinstate a cwd-dependent agy gate read without failing this test, so a reviewed repo's opt-in could be decided by whatever `.loa.config.yaml` sits in Bridgebuilder's process cwd. The suite would stay green.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the arity check with a behavioral one: create a temp dir containing `.loa.config.yaml` with `agy_opt_in: true`, `process.chdir` into it inside the test, call `validateApiKeys(models, { optIn: false, mode: "cli-only" })` and assert the google voice lands in `notPlanned`. Optionally assert `validateApiKeys(models, undefined as never)` throws rather than falling back. If `BridgebuilderConfig.repoRoot` is always set in production, drop the cwd fallback in `loaConfigPathFor` and pin a throw for `undefined` instead.

findings.description: Both diagnostics cases force `LOA_HEADLESS_MODE=cli-only` from the environment, so the routing decision for the google voice never depends on what `readAgyGate` returns for `mode` when `readError` is set. The companion unit test ('an unreadable config fails closed but says why') asserts only `optIn === false`; the mode under an unreadable config is never pinned. If the pipeline defaults mode to `prefer-api` on readError with no env override, a google voice whose on-disk config actually says `mode: cli-only` is planned by Bridgebuilder, dispatched to cheval, routed to agy, refused with `opt_in_required`, and counted as a failed planned voice.
findings.failure_mode: An unreadable `.loa.config.yaml` (for example a YAML construct BB's parser rejects but yq/python accept) with no `LOA_HEADLESS_MODE` set yields a planned-then-refused google voice and a DEGRADED verdict or strict-mode failure, instead of the 'not planned' diagnostic the sprint promises under G-1. The current tests cannot detect this because they short-circuit the mode via env.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third diagnostics case with `LOA_HEADLESS_MODE` deleted and the unclosed YAML body. Assert the gate's `mode` under readError (fail closed means treating it as `cli-only`), assert the google voice is not planned, and assert exactly one `agy gate unreadable` warn. Also assert `g.mode` in the readAgyGate readError unit test so the fail-closed claim covers both fields.

findings.description: The rewritten 'resolves catalog aliases' case introduces a reference to `TOKEN_BUDGETS["default"]`. The previous version of this case used only `getTokenBudget`, `effectiveInputBudget` and `progressiveTruncate`, and the file's import block is not part of the diff, so the identifier cannot be confirmed as imported from `../core/truncation.js` from the diff alone.
findings.failure_mode: If `TOKEN_BUDGETS` is not already imported in this file, the case fails on its first assertion with `ReferenceError: TOKEN_BUDGETS is not defined`, and the alias-clamp regression coverage for the `opus` alias is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `TOKEN_BUDGETS` is in the import list from `../core/truncation.js`. If not, add it, or express the 'row exists' check without the constant, e.g. `assert.notDeepEqual(getTokenBudget("claude-opus-5-5"), getTokenBudget("some-unknown-model"))`.

findings.description: The new 'every configured voice is not planned' throw always attributes the cause to the opt-in ('set hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true') even when agyGate.readError is set. In that case the gate failed closed because yq is missing or the YAML is unparsable, not because the operator left the key off; the thrown message is what reaches the per-PR failure record and run summary, while the correct reason exists only in an earlier logger.warn line. Additionally, the pre-existing fallback that follows (valid.length === 0 -> 'all API keys missing') still fires for the mixed case of some voices notPlanned plus the rest missing keys, which is equally misleading.
findings.failure_mode: Operator with a broken .loa.config.yaml (or no yq on PATH) and LOA_HEADLESS_MODE=cli-only sees the run fail with instructions to set agy_opt_in: true, sets it, and the run fails identically because the file still cannot be read.
findings.suggested_fix: When agyGate.readError is defined, build the thrown message from it ('agy gate unreadable: <readError>; voices routed to agy are not planned: ...') instead of the opt-in hint. Replace the length-equality check with a single valid.length === 0 check whose message lists notPlanned and missing separately.

findings.description: Inside the notPlanned loop, `if (agyGate.readError !== undefined) continue;` skips the per-voice line entirely. The generic readError warn emitted above says 'voices routed to agy are not planned' but names none of them. In strict mode this weakens the r251-1 G3 promise (every configured voice is accounted for at warn): a configured google voice silently drops with only a generic sentence that does not mention it.
findings.failure_mode: Strict-mode operator with an unreadable config and cli-only mode loses a configured voice; the only log line does not name the voice or the model id, so the verdict quality 'N/N voices' summary is smaller than configured with no attributable reason in the logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the notPlanned list (provider/modelId) to the readError warn, or keep the per-voice strict warn and only suppress the graceful info line under readError.

findings.description: MEASURED_TO_ESTIMATE_SAFETY = 1.8 encodes a property of one tokenizer (Opus 4.7+ vs BB's chars/4 estimate), but the trigger for applying it is the mere presence of a positive ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens. Any future calibrated entry inherits the 1.8 divisor regardless of its actual estimate-to-measured ratio: a model whose tokenizer matches chars/4 would be over-truncated by ~45% (160000 -> 88000), and a model with a worse ratio would be under-protected and still trip cheval's pre-flight gate. The probe record already carries the observed tokenizer_ratio per the implementation report, so the data exists to make this per-entry.
findings.failure_mode: Next calibration of a non-Opus-4.7-tokenizer model (or a non-Anthropic provider) silently gets a budget that is either far too small (review quality loss from aggressive truncation) or still too large (exit 7 rejections the ceiling was meant to prevent).
findings.suggested_fix: Record the observed ratio in ceiling_calibration (e.g. tokenizer_ratio or estimate_tokens_at_accept) and have flattenModels read it; budgetMaxInput divides by max(ratio, 1) with a small safety margin, falling back to 1.8 only for entries that have measured_input_tokens but no ratio.

findings.description: HEADER_TRUNCATION is a template literal but hardcodes the text 'MEASURED_TO_ESTIMATE_SAFETY = 1.8' instead of interpolating the constant (which is declared above it and in scope). The new bats T14 header test greps for that literal string, so changing the constant would leave the generated header and the test both asserting a stale value while budgets are computed with the new one.
findings.failure_mode: Divisor tuned to e.g. 1.6; generated truncation header, the T14 header test, and the hand-written comment in tests/unit/gen-bb-registry-codegen.bats all keep saying 1.8 while GENERATED_TOKEN_BUDGETS reflects 1.6 — a drift the regen-model-artifacts drift check cannot catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `${MEASURED_TO_ESTIMATE_SAFETY}` in the header template, and have T14 derive the expected divisor from the generated header (or from the script source) rather than a literal.

findings.description: At startup, agyGate.readError is printed only inside the `keyStatus.notPlanned.length > 0` branch, and agyGate.typeWarning is never printed. Under the fail-closed defaults (no LOA_HEADLESS_MODE, so mode falls to 'prefer-api') an unreadable config usually yields an empty notPlanned list for HTTP google voices, so startup is silent about the unreadable file. The pipeline then emits the same warn once per reviewed PR, so r251-1 G12/G14's 'said once' becomes 'said zero times at startup, N times per run'.
findings.failure_mode: Operator with agy_opt_in: "true" (string) or a malformed config sees no diagnostic in the startup banner, and discovers the misconfiguration only by reading repeated per-PR warnings in the run log.
findings.suggested_fix: In main.ts print readError and typeWarning unconditionally, once, right after the 'Multi-model: ... available' line; optionally pass a flag into executeMultiModelReview so the pipeline does not repeat it per PR.

findings.description: The three headless wire_effort classmethods (claude, codex, grok) call the instance resolver on `cls.__new__(cls)`, an object that never ran ProviderAdapter.__init__ / HeadlessCLIAdapter.__init__, and pass a SimpleNamespace in place of the catalog entry. Any `self.*` state the resolver touches now or later (config, provider name, a warn-once set for an invalid `extra.effort`/`reasoning_effort`, dict-style `entry.get(...)`) raises AttributeError. Because cheval calls wire_effort to fill `effort_effective` in the MODELINV envelope and the `--dry-run` line, that AttributeError surfaces after a successful completion or on dry-run, not in the adapter's own complete() path.
findings.failure_mode: AttributeError inside wire_effort when _resolve_effort / _resolve_reasoning_effort reads an attribute set only in __init__ (e.g. a one-time WARN path on a malformed catalog value), failing the invoke after the provider call already happened or crashing --dry-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the effort resolvers pure module-level or @staticmethod functions taking (request_effort, extra) and have both complete() and wire_effort call that function; drop the __new__ instance and the SimpleNamespace stand-in.

findings.cross_file_justification: The base default (None) is what OpenAIAdapter, BedrockAdapter, GoogleAdapter, CursorHeadlessAdapter and AgyHeadlessAdapter inherit; those adapters are not in the diff but their complete() bodies decide whether the recorded `effort_effective` matches the wire.
findings.description: Only anthropic, claude-headless, codex-headless and grok-headless override wire_effort. Every other registered adapter reports `effort_effective: null`. If any of them emit a reasoning-effort control from `request.effort` or a catalog `extra` (OpenAI `reasoning.effort`/`reasoning_effort` on gpt-5.x/o-series, Bedrock's Anthropic body builder, cursor-agent flags), the MODELINV record drifts from the body/argv, which is the exact invariant the docstring and tests/test_effort_wire_conformance.py claim to enforce.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV envelopes for openai/openai_compat/bedrock/cursor-headless dispatches record `effort_effective: null` while the request carried an effort control, so audit and cost reasoning over effort are wrong for those providers.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the conformance test iterate _ADAPTER_REGISTRY and assert, per adapter, that the effort control present in the built body/argv equals wire_effort(); add overrides (or an explicit `emits_effort = False` assertion) for every adapter so a silent default cannot pass.

findings.cross_file_justification: input_bound only reads `observed`; the writer of .run/ceiling-observed.json (the self-correction in cheval / the Anthropic adapter's context-limit handler) is outside the diff and historically mirrored the reader's `not calibrated` rule.
findings.description: The reader now lets an observed provider limit tighten a foreign-transport calibration (the Opus 5.5 entry calibrated via claude-headless). The diff does not touch the self-correction that writes observations. If that writer still skips calibrated entries (the symmetric rule the old reader had), no observation is ever recorded for claude-opus-5-5 on the HTTP route, the new branch is dead in production, and an account whose HTTP tier is below 936,000 input tokens gets a 400 on every oversize dispatch with no learning.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated ProviderContextLimitError on the HTTP route for the foreign-calibrated entry; `/loa` keeps rendering `calibrated 936000` with no observed tightening because nothing writes the observation.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the observation writer use the same predicate (`not is_calibrated(entry) or is_foreign_transport_calibration(entry)`) and add a test that a parsed context-limit rejection for a foreign-calibrated entry lands in ceiling-observed.json and lowers the next input_bound.

findings.cross_file_justification: as_envelope output is embedded in the MODELINV payload validated against .claude/data/schemas/model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json, which is not in the diff.
findings.description: as_envelope adds a new key `input_ceiling.calibration_transport` whenever the entry's calibration names a transport, which the live catalog now does for claude-opus-5-5. If the payload schema's `input_ceiling` object is closed (`additionalProperties: false`) and was not extended in this round, every Opus 5.5 HTTP dispatch produces an envelope that fails schema validation.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV write or schema test fails only for the one calibrated entry; the sprint's own schema bats suite would pass because fixtures predate the new key.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `calibration_transport` (string, optional) to the `input_ceiling` schema object and extend the envelope fixture/test with a foreign-transport decision so the additive claim is pinned.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test compares cheval._lookup_max_input_tokens (reads the host's .run/ceiling-observed.json) with input_bound(entry, max_tokens=mt) (observed=None); the diff's change to input_bound makes the calibrated entry sensitive to that host file for the first time.
findings.description: Before this round a calibrated entry ignored observations on both sides, so the comparison was host-independent for claude-opus-5-5. Now _lookup_max_input_tokens applies an observed cap for the foreign-calibrated entry while the test's expected value is computed without one. The sibling test (test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch) already pins LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH to a nonexistent file for exactly this reason; this one does not.
findings.failure_mode: The test fails on any host whose ceiling-observed.json holds an observation for claude-opus-5-5 below 936,000 (e.g. after one tier-limited HTTP rejection), passing on the developer's machine.
findings.suggested_fix: Set LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH to a nonexistent path in the test (or in the autouse fixture) and add a separate case that feeds a synthetic observation to both sides.

findings.description: _RE_CLI_TOKENS_LIMIT matches any `N tokens (limit M)` shape and records M as `limit`, the same slot _RE_INPUT_ONLY uses for the provider's input maximum. For the Claude Code pre-flight the M it captures is the total context window (1,000,000), not an input bound, and N includes the CLI's own system prompt. Downstream consumers that write `limit` as an observed input cap are protected today only because I1 (`context_window - max_tokens`) happens to clamp below it; the regex is also loose enough to match a non-context message with that shape if parse_context_limit is reached without the marker gate.
findings.failure_mode: An observation of 999,999 (or a bogus cap from an unrelated `tokens (limit …)` message) lands in ceiling-observed.json and either over-promises on a route without a derived bound or under-caps an uncalibrated/foreign-calibrated entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the CLI match in a distinct field (e.g. `context_total`) or subtract the request's max_tokens before treating it as an input limit, and anchor the regex to the CLI's wording (`the request is ~N tokens (limit M)`) so only the known pre-flight message matches.

findings.description: The three hunks labelled under providers/__init__.py are not registry code. They define pytest tests (test_ceiling_is_the_computed_value_per_entry, test_a_foreign_transport_calibration_carries_its_provenance, test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch, test_opus_5_5_has_the_1m_window_at_standard_pricing), use fixtures named http_entries/catalog/anthropic, import from the top-level cheval module, and compute REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3], which only resolves to the repository root from .claude/adapters/tests/. The supplied full-file context for providers/__init__.py shows the untouched adapter registry. The content matches tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py, which the implementation report names as the file carrying the _measured branch.
findings.failure_mode: If the hunks really landed in providers/__init__.py, importing loa_cheval.providers would pull in pytest, the cheval CLI module and the catalog path .claude/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml, breaking every adapter import. Far more likely the diff metadata is wrong, in which case the P0 escalation reviewed the registry instead of the test module and the registry review is vacuous.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with `git show --stat 059e26be` which file the hunks belong to. If the diff path is a harness artefact, re-run the review with the correct path so anchors are stable; if the test code is actually in providers/__init__.py, move it to .claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py.

findings.description: Both synthetic fixtures (_calibrated in test_ceiling_calibrated_count.py and _entry in test_ceiling_calibration_transport.py) hardcode calibrated_at 2026-10-07T09:29:07Z together with stale_after_days 90. The live catalog entry read by test_the_live_opus55_entry_is_a_foreign_transport_calibration carries the same date and window. Calibrated-ness is already derived from calibrated_at (test_transport_helpers flips it to None to get an uncalibrated entry), so it is plausible that input_bound/gate also treat a calibration past stale_after_days as not calibrated.
findings.failure_mode: If staleness is enforced by the policy, every assertion of d.calibrated is True, basis == 'calibrated', the 0.5 count trigger and the 'warn' action in these two modules starts failing on 2027-01-05 with no code change, and the live-catalog test fails as well until the entry is reprobed. CI goes red on a calendar date rather than on a regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Build calibrated_at from datetime.now(timezone.utc) in the fixtures, or set stale_after_days to a value that cannot elapse, or freeze time with a monkeypatched clock. For the live-catalog test, assert staleness explicitly and skip or xfail with a message naming the reprobe when the calibration has aged out, so the failure is self-explaining.

findings.description: The expected value in the no-kill-switch loop changed from a concrete number (CEILING_CAP or the entry's effective_input_ceiling) to input_bound(entry, max_tokens=_default_max_tokens(entry)).value. The assertion is now _lookup_max_input_tokens(...) == input_bound(...).value. If _lookup_max_input_tokens is implemented by calling input_bound with the same arguments, the comparison is policy == policy and the docstring's SDD §3.2 claim (180K under streaming) is no longer checked here. Separately, the test relies on LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH being the variable the ceiling module honours for the observed-limit file; the new transport tests never set it and pass observed= explicitly, so the name cannot be confirmed from the diff.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in input_bound (for example the 180K cap being dropped for uncalibrated entries, or observed tightening leaking into the API path) passes this test because both sides move together. If the env var name is wrong, _lookup_max_input_tokens reads the host's real .run/ceiling-observed.json while input_bound gets observed=None, and the test becomes host-state dependent: a 200000 API-route observation would make it fail only on hosts that recorded one.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one concrete expectation per branch: CEILING_CAP-capped room for uncalibrated entries and min(effective_input_ceiling, room) for measured ones, and additionally assert the basis returned by input_bound. Assert that the ceiling module exposes the env var name as a constant and use that constant in monkeypatch.setenv, or pass the observed path through a fixture that both the lookup and the test share.

findings.description: Three gaps in the provenance guard. (1) method is accepted from ('probed_api', 'probed_headless') even though the test only runs for entries whose ceiling_calibration.transport is not api; a probed_api method on a claude-headless transport is contradictory provenance and passes. (2) isinstance(cal.get('measured_input_tokens'), int) accepts True because bool subclasses int. (3) When no HTTP entry is a foreign-transport calibration the loop continues through every entry and the test passes with zero assertions, so removing the transport key from the live entry silently disables the guard rather than failing or skipping.
findings.failure_mode: A hand-edited or tool-written entry with method: probed_api, transport: claude-headless, or with measured_input_tokens: true, is accepted as auditable provenance; the foreign-transport tightening in routing.ceiling then trusts a bound whose stated origin does not match its transport. A future catalog edit that drops transport makes the test vacuous without anyone noticing.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the method to match the transport family (probed_headless for any headless transport, probed_api only for api), check type(x) is int or isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool), and count checked entries, asserting at least one or calling pytest.skip with a reason when none is foreign.

findings.description: The test pins that a calibrated entry with no counter (counter None or a failed count) dispatches with action 'warn' at an estimate of 0.6 x bound and keeps estimate.method == 'heuristic'. The module docstring states the heuristic under-counts the Opus 4.7+ tokenizer by 1.4 to 1.8 times, and the probe record in the report shows 692,678 estimated for 972,887 measured (1.40x). A heuristic estimate at or above bound/1.8 (about 0.56 x bound, roughly 520,000 for the 936,000 entry) can therefore already exceed the 1,000,000 window. The route the calibration was measured on, claude-headless under subscription auth, is exactly the route where a provider count_tokens call is typically unavailable, so the warn path is the common path there, not the fallback.
findings.failure_mode: On the headless route a request estimated between about 0.56 and 1.0 of the bound is dispatched with only a warning and is rejected by the CLI pre-flight ('Prompt is too long'), spending a round trip and producing a size failure the gate exists to prevent. The test cements warn-and-dispatch as the contract rather than a ratio-corrected estimate.
findings.suggested_fix: When the entry is calibrated and no count is available, scale the heuristic by a conservative tokenizer ratio before comparing to the bound (the probe already computes tokenizer_ratio; persist it in ceiling_calibration or default to 1.8) and preempt when the scaled estimate exceeds the bound; keep 'warn' for the band below that. Add a test that an estimate of 0.6 x bound with no counter preempts when the scaled value exceeds the bound.

findings.description: The skip condition is cal.get('transport') in (None, 'api'), but the policy as pinned by test_same_or_absent_transport_calibration_is_never_lowered_by_an_observation also treats 'API', ' api ', 'http' and '' as same-transport. If the live entry is ever written with one of those spellings the test does not skip, runs the foreign-transport assertions and fails on basis == 'observed'. The function also hardcodes max_tokens=64_000 and a 100_000 offset against whatever the live ceiling is, so a smaller future ceiling or a larger default output budget changes which invariant wins and the assertion on basis becomes wrong for reasons unrelated to the feature. The pytest.skip path itself contradicts the sprint's zero-skips acceptance criterion.
findings.failure_mode: A catalog rewrite with transport: http or API turns a should-skip case into a hard failure; a reprobe that lowers the ceiling or a default output budget change makes the I1 bound win and the basis assertion fail without any policy regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate on `not is_foreign_transport_calibration(entry)` rather than a literal tuple so the skip mirrors the policy, compute the observation offset from the actual I1 room (context_window minus the default output budget) instead of fixed numbers, and either drop the skip in favour of a hard assertion that the live entry is foreign or document the skip as the intended behaviour.

findings.description: The diff appends pytest test functions directly to the production package initializer `loa_cheval.providers.__init__`. The first decorator uses `pytest.mark.parametrize`, but this module does not import `pytest` and is imported by normal adapter code paths.
findings.failure_mode: Any runtime import of `loa_cheval.providers` will raise `NameError: name 'pytest' is not defined` at module import time, preventing cheval/provider initialization in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these tests into a test module under `.claude/adapters/tests/`, or if this hunk was intended for an existing test file, apply it there instead of the production `loa_cheval.providers` package initializer.

findings.description: The first hunk is attributed to `loa_cheval/providers/__init__.py` but its content is three pytest functions (`test_invalid_extra_effort_warns_once_per_model_and_reason`, `test_invalid_extra_effort_on_an_http_entry_is_not_read_and_not_warned`, `test_extra_rung_iterates_both_keys_in_the_adapter_order`) with pre-context `def test_modelinv_schema_declares_effort_source()` at line 393. The supplied full file for that path is the ~115-line adapter registry: no `import pytest`, no `cheval`, no `_ns`, no `caplog`, and no line 393. The hunk cannot apply to that file. Conversely, the registry as shown already contains an r251-1 change (`adapter_class_for_type`, documented as what `cheval._effort_on_wire` calls) that does not appear anywhere in the diff.
findings.failure_mode: Two readings, both unmergeable. (a) If the hunk really lands in `providers/__init__.py`, the `@pytest.mark.parametrize` decorator raises `NameError: pytest` at import, so `from loa_cheval.providers import ...` fails and every cheval invocation (HTTP and CLI) dies before dispatch. (b) If the path is mislabeled (the tests belong in `tests/test_effort_catalog_default.py`), the actual production change to the registry (`adapter_class_for_type`, the function `_effort_on_wire` now depends on) has not been presented for review, and the new resolver tests cannot be located or verified against their helper (`_ns`).
findings.suggested_fix: Re-emit the diff with the three tests under their real file (the module that defines `_ns` and `test_modelinv_schema_declares_effort_source`), and include the real `providers/__init__.py` hunk that adds `adapter_class_for_type` (also add it to `__all__`). Confirm with `python -c 'import loa_cheval.providers'` from `.claude/adapters` that the registry imports cleanly.

findings.description: `_http_body` returns `cap.body or {}` and `_capture_post` sets `body=None` whenever the transport was called with a non-dict body (for example a `json.dumps`-serialized string, which is the normal shape for Bedrock InvokeModel) or with a dict lacking `messages`/`contents`/`input`. An empty dict makes `_emitted` return `None` for Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI and pass the Google `'effort' not in repr` assertion. Since `_effort_on_wire` also returns `None` for bedrock, openai, openai_compat and google types, `recorded == emitted` holds with nothing inspected. The `hasattr(mod, name)` guard in `_offline` likewise silently skips patching when an adapter imports the transport under another name, in which case the test makes a real HTTPS call with the fake keys.
findings.failure_mode: The file's stated guarantee (MODELINV `effort_effective` equals the wire value for EVERY catalog model) is vacuous for every non-Anthropic HTTP route. If `BedrockAdapter` or `OpenAIAdapter` forwards `request.effort` (e.g. `output_config.effort` or `reasoning.effort`), MODELINV records `effort_effective: null` while the wire carries `high`, and this suite stays green. Where the stub is not installed, unit tests hit the network and fail on hosts without egress.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_http_body`, `pytest.fail` when `cap.body is None` instead of returning `{}`; in `_capture_post`, also accept `str`/`bytes` bodies and `json.loads` them. Replace the `hasattr` guard with a hard `monkeypatch.setattr(mod, name, ...)` for the known transport symbol per adapter (raising if absent) so a rename cannot un-stub a transport.

findings.description: This new test locks in that, for `openai:codex-headless` and `xai:grok-build`, a catalog `extra.reasoning_effort: low` beats an explicit caller `effort="high"` on the wire, and that `_effort_on_wire` reports `low`. FR-2's documented precedence (and `resolve_effort` as tested in the first hunk) is caller > catalog default > extra > none. So `--effort high` is resolved as `(high, caller)`, `--dry-run` prints `effort: high (caller)`, yet the Codex/Grok adapters emit `low`. No warning is raised for the override; only `effort_effective` in MODELINV discloses it.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who passes `--effort high` to a Codex or Grok route gets `low` reasoning silently, and the dry-run output affirmatively misstates what will be sent. Future readers will treat this test as the spec rather than as documentation of a gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Either have `CodexHeadlessAdapter`/`GrokHeadlessAdapter._build_command` prefer `request.effort` when it is set (falling back to `extra.reasoning_effort`), which makes the wire match the resolver and lets this test assert `high`; or, if extra must win for those CLIs, emit the existing once-per-(model, reason) WARN from `resolve_effort` when `effort_source == 'caller'` and `_effort_on_wire` differs, and print the effective value on the dry-run line.

findings.cross_file_justification: The catalog hunk changes `sample_size` from null to 5 on a `source: operator_set` entry. The schema's previous `sample_size` description codified the invariant 'null when source != empirical_probe', so consumers outside this diff (loa-status LSP-5 calibrated branch, gen-bb-registry codegen, cycle-124-anthropic-catalog bats, tools/ceiling-probe-live.py's own write/read) may have inferred empirical-probe provenance from a non-null `sample_size`. Only the description text was relaxed in the schema; no structural rule ties `sample_size` to `source`/`probe_outcome`.
findings.description: `sample_size` moves from `null` to `5` while `source` stays `operator_set` and `probe_outcome: partial` is added. The schema change only rewrites the description; nothing in the schema expresses the new rule (non-null `sample_size` allowed with `operator_set`, `probe_outcome` expected when `method: probed_*`). Readers that keyed provenance on `sample_size != null` will now present this hand-vouched partial probe as an empirical probe, and generated artifacts (BB registry/truncation) must be regenerated for the new field or the drift gate fails.
findings.failure_mode: Status/registry output misreports calibration confidence for Opus 5.5 (e.g. 'probed, n=5' rather than 'operator_set, partial'), or `regen-model-artifacts.sh --check` reports drift because the generated TS was not refreshed after the catalog edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep consumers of `sample_size` and `ceiling_calibration.source` (`loa-status.sh`, `gen-bb-registry*`, `ceiling-probe-live.py`, catalog bats) and switch any provenance inference to `source`/`probe_outcome`. Add a schema `if/then` so `probe_outcome` is required when `method` starts with `probed_`, and re-run `tools/regen-model-artifacts.sh` to confirm the catalog edit is drift-free.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test pins the charge policy implemented in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py (charge_basis / provider_rejection_unbilled in the attempt loop that _classify feeds), which is what the --budget-usd cap is computed from.
findings.description: The test now asserts that every `transient` attempt and the size rejection are `provider_rejection_unbilled` with `charged_usd == 0`, keyed solely on the CLI error body lacking `total_cost_usd`. That is correct for pre-processing rejections (400 prompt-too-long, 429, 529, CLI pre-flight) but the `transient` class per the sprint report also covers network errors, and likely attempt timeouts. A connection drop or timeout after the provider accepted a ~900K-token request is billed for input (~$4.50 at the $5/MTok cache-write rate) yet the probe records $0 and keeps retrying, so up to three such attempts (~$13.50) are invisible to a $20 cap. The `huge` mode has the same shape: the model ran and produced >1 MiB of output but no cost is parsed, and the diff asserts nothing about its charge. The fake gained `FAKE_ERR_COST` to simulate an error body that does carry a cost, but no test in the diff uses it, so the only path that would catch a billed error is unverified.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended live probe over Bedrock hits network/timeout failures mid-request at large sizes; each is charged $0, the bisection continues, and real spend exceeds --budget-usd by several dollars while the record reports spent_usd under the cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict `provider_rejection_unbilled` to statuses/messages known to be rejected before processing (CLI pre-flight, 400/413 context limit, 429, 529, 5xx with an api_error_status). For timeouts, connection errors, and SubprocessOutputCapExceeded, charge the step's input estimate (measured or requested size × cache-write rate) unless the CLI body carries total_cost_usd. Add a test that sets FAKE_ERR_COST and asserts the error attempt's charge_basis is the CLI cost, and assert the `huge` sample's charged_usd is non-zero.

findings.description: The recording fake gains four new knobs — modes `bedrock_flaky` and `bedrock_tpm` (the Bedrock "Too many tokens, please wait before trying again." message, once transiently and once persistently at the oversize boundary), `FAKE_RETRY_AFTER` (a retry-after hint on the 429 text), and `FAKE_ERR_COST` — but no test in this diff sets any of them. These are precisely the behaviours the r251-1 triage lists as fixed ("throttle-vs-context precedence", "TPM backoff", charging). The Bedrock throttle text is ambiguous between a per-minute throttle and a context rejection; without a test, whether the probe treats a persistent `bedrock_tpm` at the boundary as `token_limit` (partial) rather than `context_limit` (clean) is unverified, and the retry-after hint path is dead fixture code.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in the Bedrock throttle classification or retry-after handling passes the suite; a persistent Bedrock throttle at the boundary could be written to the catalog as a clean context-limit measurement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tests: `bedrock_flaky` → one transient attempt then success, short backoff schedule; `bedrock_tpm` at a 300K limit → failure_class token_limit, TPM schedule, outcome partial; `FAKE_RETRY_AFTER=90` → the sleep honours the hint over the fixed schedule; `FAKE_ERR_COST` → the error attempt is charged. Or drop the unused knobs from the fake.

findings.description: `_adapters_base()` does an unconditional `sys.path.insert(0, ROOT/.claude/adapters)` from inside `test_output_past_the_1mb_cap_raises_and_kills_the_group` and never removes it, so the mutation outlives the test and leaks into every later test in the session (and into other modules under the same worker). The `tool` fixture already imports `loa_cheval.providers.base` transitively, so the insert is also redundant. Separately, the test's name says the process group is killed, but nothing asserts the child is gone after `SubprocessOutputCapExceeded` is raised; the earlier version also checked the stderr cap, which is no longer covered.
findings.failure_mode: Later tests in the same pytest session may import a different copy of a module via the prepended path, producing order-dependent failures that do not reproduce in isolation; the kill-the-group claim is untested so an orphaned 3 MB writer would not be detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the helper with `monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(...)` or import the exception through the already-loaded tool module (e.g. `tool.SubprocessOutputCapExceeded`). Assert the child's pid is dead after the raise (os.kill(pid, 0) → ProcessLookupError) or rename the test; add a stderr-overflow case.

findings.description: This test deliberately runs `tool.main()` on the claude-headless transport WITHOUT the `fake` fixture, with a 400K-token upper bound and a $20 budget, and relies on an ambient CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN sentinel (asserted separately by test_p11_the_module_default_binary_is_a_sentinel_that_does_not_exist) to make the spawn fail. The test receives `monkeypatch` but only uses it for argv; it never pins CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN itself. The reviewer context shows the suites were run under `env -u CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN`, which indicates the module-level sentinel does not override an inherited value. An operator who uses the CLI route legitimately exports CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to the real binary; in that shell the sentinel test fails loudly but this test still executes and reaches a real `claude -p`.
findings.failure_mode: On a developer or CI host with CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN exported to a real claude binary (and Bedrock/Anthropic credentials present), the unit test sends real 400K-token prompts and bisects downward until the $20 budget or a result is reached: real spend and real provider calls from `pytest`, exactly the zero-spend guarantee the P11 fix claims to make fail-closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside the test, set `monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN", str(tmp_path / "loa-probe-no-real-cli"))` (and `monkeypatch.delenv` any AWS/Anthropic credential vars) before calling `main()`, so the fail-on-spawn property does not depend on import-time state or the invoking shell. Consider also making the module-level sentinel an unconditional assignment rather than setdefault, or an autouse fixture that forces it unless the `fake` fixture is active.

findings.cross_file_justification: test_p7_stdin_is_delivered_and_the_child_leads_its_own_group pins that `_run_capped` places the child in its own process group (and, if implemented via start_new_session, its own session). test_an_interrupt_after_paid_steps_still_writes_the_record is the only KeyboardInterrupt coverage, and it monkeypatches `_run_capped` away entirely, so the interrupt never occurs while a real child is running. The combination leaves the interrupt-during-communicate path of `_run_capped` in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py unexercised.
findings.description: Once the child leads its own group/session, a terminal Ctrl-C delivers SIGINT only to the Python parent, not to `claude -p`. If `_run_capped` kills the group only on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (the case the P7 test exercises) and not on KeyboardInterrupt/BaseException, the operator's interrupt raises inside `communicate()`, main() writes the record and exits 130, and the orphaned CLI child continues to completion in its own session. The diff's tests cannot detect this because the interrupt test replaces `_run_capped` before any child exists.
findings.failure_mode: Operator presses ^C mid-attempt: the probe exits 130 with `stop: interrupted`, but the real `claude -p` request still completes against the provider, billing the full attempt, and the process lingers as an orphan until the API call returns. The record's `interrupted_estimate` charge happens to cover the cost, but the child is not stopped and any subsequent re-run overlaps with it (ITPM contention, the exact 429 class the TPM backoff logic then has to absorb).
findings.suggested_fix: In `_run_capped`, wrap the `communicate()` call in `try/finally` (or `except BaseException: os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL); raise`) so the group is killed on any exit path, not just TimeoutExpired. Add a test alongside the P7 pair that spawns the GRANDCHILD wrapper via the real `_run_capped`, sends SIGINT to the test process (or raises KeyboardInterrupt via a timer/signal handler) during the wait, and asserts the grandchild is dead.

findings.description: The pidfile wait loop runs only after `_run_capped` has already raised TimeoutExpired, i.e. after the wrapper has been killed; the pidfile can no longer appear at that point, so the 10-second poll is dead time. If the 2-second cap fires before the wrapper has executed `open(...).write(...)` (slow interpreter start on a loaded runner), the test burns the 10 s deadline and then crashes with FileNotFoundError at `int(pidfile.read_text())` instead of a readable assertion. In that same scenario the grandchild may already have been spawned by Popen but its pid is unknown, so the cleanup `os.kill(gc, 9)` never runs and a 300-second sleeper leaks if the group kill under test is in fact broken.
findings.failure_mode: Flaky, hard-to-diagnose failure on slow CI (FileNotFoundError with no indication that the timeout simply pre-empted the pidfile write), plus a possible orphaned sleeper for 5 minutes when the kill path regresses.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the wrapper write the pidfile before anything slow (or have the test poll for the pidfile in a thread started before `_run_capped`, with a timeout longer than the 2 s cap); replace the bare `read_text()` with `assert pidfile.exists(), "wrapper never reached the pidfile write within the cap"`; and increase the cap to something comfortably above interpreter start (e.g. 5 s) so the test measures group-kill behaviour rather than spawn latency.

findings.description: `--tier` changed from `default="unverified"` to `default=None` while the documented API transport default remains `unverified`. Unless every API path below now normalizes `None` before use, invoking the probe with the default `--transport api` no longer supplies the intended tier and can either omit the request tier or fail validation downstream.
findings.failure_mode: A default API probe run behaves differently from the CLI contract: `--tier` is no longer `unverified` by default, so the transport may use an unintended account tier or reject the call, violating the documented flag behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep argparse default as `"unverified"` for API transport, or normalize `args.tier = "unverified"` before any API transport logic while still rejecting `--tier` for `claude-headless` if that is required.

findings.description: (Content is tools/ceiling-probe-live.py despite the diff header.) The throttle-wins precedence `_THROTTLE.search(full) and (is_context_limit_message(full) or is_token_limit_message(full))` is now evaluated over `full`, which concatenates the error `result`, the api_status tag and the ENTIRE stderr (up to 1 MB); previously only 300 chars were examined. Any `throttl`, `please wait`, `rate limit`, `tokens per min` or bare `429` anywhere in stderr (wrapper banner, CLI notice, an unrelated earlier log line) flips a genuine context-limit rejection into `transient token_limit`, costing up to 4 attempts / 140 s per step, and if it persists it is recorded as `failure_class: token_limit`, which forces outcome `partial` even though the real bracket was a context-limit rejection. Separately, the bare-429 alternative `(?<![\d,.])429(?![\d,.])` also rejects a sentence-final period, so `... returned status 429.` is not recognised as a throttle marker.
findings.failure_mode: A real size rejection is retried on the TPM schedule and then mis-bracketed; a clean probe degrades to `partial` for a reason unrelated to the model; a 429 that ends a sentence loses the throttle precedence and may be classified as a size rejection with no retry (the exact r251-1 regression the rule was added to prevent).
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the throttle precedence on the structured error only (`result` + api_status), or require the throttle marker within a short window (e.g. 200 chars) of the context/token marker rather than anywhere in 1 MB of stderr. Change the 429 lookahead to `(?!\d|[,.]\d)` so trailing punctuation is allowed while `429,000` / `429.5` are still excluded. Add tests: a context-limit `result` with stderr containing "please wait" must classify `size`; "status 429." must match the throttle marker.

findings.cross_file_justification: `_run_capped` (in the diff) replaced `subprocess.run(input=bytes, timeout=)` with `run_subprocess_pgkill(cmd, input=prompt, ..., max_bytes=_CAPTURE_CAP)` from loa_cheval.providers.base. The input is now a str, and the failure contract changed: the helper raises `SubprocessOutputCapExceeded` on the cap and whatever it raises on timeout, which may not be `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. The step loop that must map these to an `other` sample is not in the diff.
findings.description: The docstring promises a timeout kills the process group and that output past the cap 'maps to `other`', but the mapping lives in the step loop outside the diff. The unit tests described in the report stub `_run_capped` with canned (rc, stdout, stderr), and the only live run (Task 1.5) predates this change, so the new `run_subprocess_pgkill` integration has never executed against a real CLI. Two things are unverified: (1) the helper accepts a str `input` (the old code passed bytes); (2) the step catches the helper's actual exception types rather than `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`.
findings.failure_mode: If the step still catches only `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, a CLI timeout propagates as an unexpected exception: the bisection ends with `stop: interrupted`, exit 1, and the attempt is charged as interrupted rather than recorded as a timeout `other` sample at the same size. If the helper expects bytes, every attempt fails before spawn and the probe never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `run_subprocess_pgkill`'s input type and the exact exceptions it raises on timeout and on the cap; make the step catch exactly those (and `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` for safety) and record `other` with `timeout: true` / `output_cap_exceeded: true` charged at the estimate. Add one test that patches `run_subprocess_pgkill` to raise each exception and asserts an `other` sample is recorded and the bisection continues/stops per spec, not an interrupted record.

findings.description: `--tier` default changed from `"unverified"` to `None` so the headless transport can detect an explicitly passed api-only flag. The api-transport write path in the same file (not in the diff) previously received the string and wrote/compared it. The help text promises "(default unverified)" but no `args.tier or "unverified"` substitution is visible in the diff.
findings.failure_mode: A default `--transport api --write-catalog` run writes `tier: None` into the catalog (or fails a `_TIERS` lookup/validation) at the write step, after the paid bisection has completed. The report's claim 'API path unchanged' does not cover a run with no `--tier` if the test passes `--tier` explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve `tier = args.tier if args.tier is not None else "unverified"` once at the top of the api branch (or set the default inside the api dispatcher) and add an api-path test that runs with no `--tier` and asserts the written tier is `unverified`.

findings.description: `probe_outcome` and `sample_size` are new REQUIRED keyword-only parameters with no defaults, and the function raises ValueError for anything but `clean`/`partial` or a non-int sample size. It is invoked at the very end of a paid run by `_main_cli` (not in the diff) and was also used ad hoc by the lead for the Task 1.5 write. Any caller still on the old signature raises TypeError at that point; a `partial` outcome without `force_partial` raises ValueError. The docstring says the catalog is never written on interrupt but says nothing about an exception raised by the catalog write itself after a completed bisection.
findings.failure_mode: A `--write-catalog` run completes the bisection (spend incurred), then crashes with TypeError/ValueError at the write. If the record is written only after the catalog write, the record is lost too and the spend has no artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify `_main_cli` passes `probe_outcome=record["outcome"]`, `sample_size=len(accepted)+len(rejected)` and `force_partial=args.write_partial_as_operator_set`. Write the record BEFORE attempting the catalog write and wrap the write so a ValueError/TypeError is reported (exit 1) with the record intact. Add a `_main_cli` clean-path test that goes through `--write-catalog` end to end rather than calling `write_catalog_operator_set` directly.

findings.description: The new TPM rule says a token-budget 429 that persists 'once the window was waited out' is a size rejection (`failure_class: token_limit`), but the same spec caps total sleep per step at `_RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S = 180` and honours a `retry-after` hint only 'when longer' up to that cap. When the hint exceeds the remaining cap (org-level ITPM pressure regularly yields hints above 60 s), the window has NOT been waited out, yet the persisting 429 still becomes a size rejection that steers the bisection downward. Separately, a `token_limit` size rejection reflects the account's per-minute budget, not the model's context window. The record's `partial` outcome and the catalog's new `probe_outcome: partial` do not say which failure class bracketed the bound, so an operator using `--write-partial-as-operator-set` cannot see that the bound is TPM-shaped.
findings.failure_mode: A bound that is an artefact of the account's ITPM rather than the model's ceiling is written as `operator_set` and governs production routing; with a long retry-after the bisection moves below the true ceiling without ever having retried outside the window.
findings.suggested_fix: When the hint exceeds the remaining cap, classify the persisting 429 as `other` (transient exhausted), not `size`. Record the bracketing `failure_class` in the record and in `ceiling_calibration` (e.g. `bracket: context_limit | token_limit`), and refuse or loudly warn on `force_partial` when the bracket is `token_limit`.

findings.description: The diff header names `.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py` (index 6e084077..8e034532) but every hunk is `tools/ceiling-probe-live.py`: the module docstring, `_run_capped`, `_classify`, `_classify_unguarded`, `write_catalog_operator_set` and `main`'s argparse. The test-file changes the report credits for r251-1 (TPM backoff schedule, throttle-vs-context precedence, interrupt record, pgkill, api-flag usage errors, required `probe_outcome`/`sample_size`) are therefore not in the review bundle, and the production tool is being reviewed under a test-file path.
findings.failure_mode: The r251-1 behaviours ship with unreviewed and possibly absent tests; review anchors resolve to the wrong file, so findings cannot be traced to the real location.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the review diff from the commit for both paths (`git show 059e26be -- tools/ceiling-probe-live.py .claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py`) and rerun the review on the test file to confirm coverage of each r251-1 behaviour listed above.

findings.description: The new preflight dry-run calls write_catalog_operator_set(..., ceiling=1).
