That exercises the writer with a bogus ceiling rather than a minimally valid probe ceiling, so any catalog path that enforces the I2/output-budget clamp can fail before the probe starts even though a real post-probe write would have been valid.
findings.failure_mode: Running the CLI with --transport claude-headless --write-catalog can exit 2 with 'no call made, nothing spent' for a valid catalog, making the write path unusable. This violates the intended behavior of only rejecting catalogs that cannot accept the eventual operator-set write.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a syntactically valid dry-run ceiling that satisfies the same clamp invariants as a real write, for example default_output_budget + 1 or the requested max probe ceiling if available, rather than 1. Keep the dry-run non-mutating.

findings.description: The r251-1 P6 pre-spend dry-run opens --write-catalog read-only and calls write_catalog_operator_set() on the text, but never checks that the final _write_text_atomic() can land (directory not writable, read-only file, temp-file creation in the catalog's directory). The comment claims 'a write that cannot land must fail before any spend'; only parse/clamp/field failures are caught before spend.
findings.failure_mode: A run against a catalog in a read-only checkout or a directory the user cannot write to passes the dry-run, spends the full budget on the bisection, and then fails with 'catalog not written: Permission denied' at the very end (clean path or the forced partial path), leaving the operator with a record but no catalog write — the exact outcome P6 was meant to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: In the dry-run block also verify writability: os.access(os.path.dirname(args.write_catalog) or '.', os.W_OK) and os.access(args.write_catalog, os.W_OK), or create-and-remove a tempfile in the target directory the same way _write_text_atomic does; return 2 with 'no call made, nothing spent' on failure.

findings.description: record['written_ceiling'] and the new record['written_probe_outcome'] are set as soon as new_catalog is computed, and the record is serialized to --output before _write_text_atomic() runs. The forced-partial branch then catches OSError from _write_text_atomic and returns 1 without amending the already-written record.
findings.failure_mode: When the catalog write fails after the record has been written, the persisted JSON report asserts written_ceiling=N / written_probe_outcome=partial while the catalog is unchanged. Anyone reading the report (the sprint evidence trail, a later re-probe decision) sees a write that never happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Perform the catalog write before serializing the record (or set written_ceiling/written_probe_outcome only after _write_text_atomic succeeds, and on failure set record['error'] and re-write the record file). Apply the same ordering to the clean path.

findings.description: `if errors: record['error'] = errors[0]` runs first; the new forced-but-no-verified-accept branch then unconditionally overwrites record['error'] with 'catalog not written: --write-partial-as-operator-set but no verified accept to vouch for' without appending to `errors`. The exit code still follows `errors` (return 1), while the record and the stderr `why` text name a different cause.
findings.failure_mode: A run that stopped with an `other` failure (e.g. the CLI could not be spawned) and was invoked with --write-partial-as-operator-set exits 1 but its record's `error` field no longer names the actual failure; the original error text is lost from the only durable artifact.
findings.suggested_fix: Only set record['error'] in the forced branch when not already set (record.setdefault), or store it under a separate key such as record['write_skipped'], keeping record['error'] bound to errors[0].

findings.description: After a successful forced write (--write-partial-as-operator-set, _write_text_atomic landed, 'written anyway as operator_set' printed), control falls through to `return 1 if errors else 3`. Exit 3 has until now meant 'partial — nothing written to the catalog'; the same code is now returned both when nothing was written and when the catalog was modified.
findings.failure_mode: Any wrapper (sprint runner, regen script, CI step) that treats exit 3 as 'no catalog change, skip regen' will skip regenerating Bridgebuilder's registry/truncation artifacts after the catalog actually changed, producing the drift that regen-model-artifacts.sh --check is meant to catch; conversely a wrapper treating non-zero as failure discards a successful write.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 0 (or a distinct documented code) when the forced write lands, and keep 3 only for 'partial, nothing written'. Document the code in the module docstring/--help.

findings.description: The outer `except BaseException as e` around the bisection converts every exception — including programming defects (TypeError in _classify, KeyError in next_target) and SystemExit — into stop='interrupted', records only f'{type}: {e}', and exits 1. The traceback is never printed, and a SystemExit's code is discarded.
findings.failure_mode: A defect in the bisection surfaces as 'interrupted (KeyError: 'size_measured')' on stderr with no traceback and no way to localize it; the record is kept (good) but the operator cannot diagnose the tool failure that just consumed budget. sys.exit(2) raised from a helper becomes exit 1.
findings.suggested_fix: In the handler, `if not isinstance(e, KeyboardInterrupt): traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)`; propagate SystemExit's code (return e.code if isinstance(e, SystemExit)); consider re-raising non-KeyboardInterrupt exceptions after the record has been written.

findings.description: The token_limit → size reclassification requires `waited >= _TPM_WINDOW_S`, where `waited` is the sum of sleeps only. _retry_wait() clamps each sleep to `_RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S - waited`, so `waited` can never exceed the cap and reaches the window only if _RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S >= _TPM_WINDOW_S and the schedule sums to it within _TPM_ATTEMPTS-1 sleeps. With fractional retry_after_s hints, `waited + (cap - waited)` can accumulate to 59.999… and miss the `>=` by floating-point error. The attempts' own wall-clock (the CLI round-trip) is not counted, so the 'only Ns were waited — the 60s window was not cleared' message can be false when far more than 60s elapsed.
findings.failure_mode: A tokens-per-minute-bounded account ends every step in kind='other' (bisection stops) instead of the intended 'size'/'token_limit' (bisection continues downward), or stops with a misleading 'window not cleared' detail, depending on constants not visible in this diff and on float accumulation.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure the window by wall-clock: record time.monotonic() at the first token_limit 429 of the step and compare `monotonic() - first_429 >= _TPM_WINDOW_S` (integer seconds, or with a small tolerance); assert at import time that _RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S >= _TPM_WINDOW_S and sum(_TPM_BACKOFF_S[:_TPM_ATTEMPTS-1]) >= _TPM_WINDOW_S so the reclassification branch is reachable.

findings.description: The Opus 5.5 ceiling bullet states two different current values for Bridgebuilder's generated input budget in the same paragraph. The retained first sentence says in present tense that 'Bridgebuilder's generated budget for the entry is 916,000'. The appended provenance text then says the generated budget 'divides by 1.8 (≈508,000 for this entry, from 916,000)'. Only one of these is the value in `truncation.generated.ts` after review round r251-1.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or later maintainer reading the CHANGELOG to confirm what Bridgebuilder budgets for `claude-opus-5-5` gets a stale figure first and a corrected figure later with no marker that the first is superseded. Downstream docs or tests written from the first sentence would pin 916,000 against a tree that generates ≈508,000.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the first mention as history ('Bridgebuilder's generated budget before the units fix was 916,000') or delete it, so the bullet carries one current value (≈508,000) and one explanation of the 1.8 divisor.

findings.description: The units-gap mitigation described in the ceiling bullet is scoped to routes with a count endpoint: 'on a calibrated entry cheval now asks the provider's free count_tokens once the estimate passes half the bound'. The bullet also says Bridgebuilder gets a 1.8 divisor 'because it has no count endpoint before building the prompt'. The headless CLI route is in the same position as Bridgebuilder (no count endpoint, cheval's chars-based estimate is the only pre-dispatch gate), yet the text applies the full 936,000 bound to it with neither mitigation. That route is the transport the calibration was measured on. With the documented 1.4x to 1.8x under-count, a request cheval estimates anywhere from roughly 555,000 to 936,000 tokens can exceed the CLI's 1,000,000 pre-flight window. The bullet describes how the probe tool classifies that CLI rejection but says nothing about how cheval's production headless adapter classifies it (ProviderContextLimitError with no walk and no breaker count, or a generic failure).
findings.failure_mode: Large `opus` prompts routed to `claude-headless` pass cheval's gate, spawn the CLI, and fail at the CLI's own pre-flight. Under the previous 180,000 bound cheval refused these pre-dispatch with a clear ceiling message. If the adapter does not map the CLI's 'limit 1000000' text to the context-limit class, the failure is walked to the next voice with the same payload and counts toward the breaker, the exact behaviour cycle-126 designed around.
findings.suggested_fix: Either apply the same measured-unit divisor to the headless route's effective bound (mirroring the Bridgebuilder rule) or document and test that `claude_headless_adapter` maps the CLI pre-flight rejection to ProviderContextLimitError with the not-walked, no-breaker handling. State whichever holds in the bullet next to the count_tokens sentence.

findings.description: The ceiling bullet says the headless measurement 'governs the HTTP entry too' and discloses the self-heal for an HTTP route that turns out narrower. It does not disclose the pricing consequence. The cycle-126 bullet in the same hunk records that every Anthropic HTTP 5-family entry carries `pricing.long_context` with `verified: false` and that `calculate_total_cost` applies the multipliers above the threshold. With the previous 180,000 bound no HTTP request could cross the 200,000 long-context threshold. With 936,000 an HTTP `opus` caller with a 500,000-token prompt is now dispatched at the premium tier instead of being refused, on a pricing row the catalog itself marks unverified. No WARN, budget pre-check, or operator note is mentioned for the first crossing.
findings.failure_mode: Callers whose prompts previously failed fast at the ceiling now succeed at roughly double input pricing, with the ledger marking the row `long_context: true` after the fact. The cost exposure is silent until `cost-report.sh` is run, and the multiplier applied is one the catalog has not verified against the vendor's published tier.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the bullet stating that HTTP requests above 200,000 tokens are now reachable and billed under the unverified `pricing.long_context` multipliers. Consider a one-time WARN (or a budget check) when the pre-dispatch estimate or count_tokens result crosses `pricing.long_context.threshold` on an entry whose long-context pricing is `verified: false`.

findings.description: The supplied diff contains no changed lines. The CHANGELOG hunk (@@ -19,2 +19,2 @@) is labelled part 2/3 of one hunk and shows only the pre-existing cycle-126 bullet as context; part 3/3 (@@ -21,3 +21,3 @@) has a header and no body; docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md has an index line and no hunk. None of the code the implementation report describes is present: resolve_effort / _effort_on_wire and the three CompletionRequest sites in cheval.py, the agy gate in agy_headless_adapter.py and agy-gate-lib.sh, write_catalog_operator_set and i2_clamped in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py, build_headless_argv, the claude-opus-5-5 catalog entry, or the schema additions. The report says the round touched 69 files.
findings.failure_mode: A consumer of this dissent reads a near-empty findings list as a second-voice pass on the sprint's code. It is not one; the code was never in the review input, so every BLOCKING-class risk in those files is unexamined here.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run the dissent with the full diff of the sprint's commits (f43949d6, 8ad37c55, 059e26be), e.g. adversarial-review.sh --diff-range <base>...<head>, so the code paths named in the report are in scope. Do not count this run toward voices_succeeded for the sprint's code review.

findings.cross_file_justification: The changed lines of this CHANGELOG hunk (the cycle-127 bullets, per the implementation report) document the catalog write of the 936,000 operator_set bound and the Task 1.5 decision; the catalog entry is where that documented behaviour lives and where cheval's HTTP adapter and Bridgebuilder read it. This finding rests on the report's own account, not on code I could read.
findings.description: The probe tool's stated contract is that only a clean outcome with --write-catalog writes probed_ceiling / effective_input_ceiling. The live run's outcome was partial and the entry was written by calling write_catalog_operator_set() directly from the lead's shell. The measurement was taken through claude-bedrock (CLI 2.1.292, us-east-1 global) and recorded on the claude-opus-5-5 entry, which is the HTTP (api.anthropic.com) entry the HTTP adapter and Bridgebuilder budget against; the CLI hop is the separate claude-headless entry. Round 1 acknowledged this as is_foreign_transport_calibration but made the HTTP bound tighten only after 'a verified observation on the HTTP route'. That is reactive: the first HTTP request sized between that route's real limit and 936,000 is sent and rejected by the provider before anything tightens. The CALIBRATED_COUNT_NEAR_BOUND count_tokens pre-gate fixes estimation units, not the per-route context limit, so it does not catch this case.
findings.failure_mode: On a host whose HTTP route for claude-opus-5-5 does not accept ~936K input (no 1M-context entitlement or beta header on the direct API), the first large review on that route fails at the provider. For a dissent that is a walked-on or dropped voice; for Bridgebuilder a failed call; repeated once per host until the reactive tightening records the observation.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the calibration to the transport it was measured on: apply the 936,000 bound to claude-headless / bedrock hops and keep the prior HTTP bound on claude-opus-5-5 until a probe runs through the HTTP transport (the tool already has an API path). If one entry must carry both, have the loader WARN once when is_foreign_transport_calibration is true and the HTTP hop appears in a chain, and have the probe tool refuse an operator_set write from a partial outcome unless an explicit --accept-partial flag names the decision, so the bypass is in the record rather than in a shell session.

findings.description: The agy routing rule documented in the changelog contradicts the SDD added in this same diff. CHANGELOG says a Google voice under `prefer-api` with no Google key is an agy route, while `grimoires/loa/sdd.md` D-1.9 says under `prefer-api` with no Google key the HTTP hop fails on credentials before any agy hop and key presence is not part of the rule.
findings.failure_mode: This leaves the normative operator docs specifying two incompatible planner behaviors for the same config: either skip as `opt_in_required` and walk on, or fail/report `no_credentials`. Implementers and tests following the changelog can produce the wrong `planned`/failure classification for Google `prefer-api` fallback chains.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the changelog use the same rule as SDD D-1.9: agy-routed means the literal `gemini-headless` hop or a Google voice under effective `cli-only`; under `prefer-api` with no Google key, classify the HTTP hop as `no_credentials` before any agy hop.

findings.cross_file_justification: CHANGELOG and SDD D-1.9 are both in this diff and give two different definitions of the single shared predicate routes_to_agy.
findings.description: The CHANGELOG defines the agy route as three cases: the literal gemini-headless hop, a Google voice under effective cli-only, OR 'a Google voice under prefer-api with no Google key resolvable'. SDD D-1.9 in the same diff defines routes_to_agy(model, mode) with only the first two cases and explicitly states 'key presence is not part of the rule' (the HTTP hop fails on no_credentials first). The predicate signature carries no key input, so the CHANGELOG's third clause cannot be what the shipped predicate computes. FR-1.5 requires one predicate; the diff publishes two definitions of it.
findings.failure_mode: Operators configuring prefer-api without a Google key read the CHANGELOG and expect the voice to be reported as not planned with reason opt_in_required (and expect setting agy_opt_in true to be the remedy), while the planners actually report no_credentials on the HTTP hop. Conformance tests written from the CHANGELOG wording would disagree with tests written from D-1.9.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the prefer-api/no-key clause from the CHANGELOG bullet (or, if the planners really do treat it as an agy route, amend D-1.9 and the predicate signature). Make the CHANGELOG sentence match the D-1.9 wording verbatim: literal gemini-headless hop, or a Google voice under effective cli-only.

findings.description: Within the same CHANGELOG bullet the unchanged context line still says 'Bridgebuilder's budget for it is 916,000 input tokens' while the added text says 'Bridgebuilder's budget for the entry is the bound divided by 1.8 (≈508,000 estimated tokens)'. Both cannot be true. The added formula is also wrong on its own terms: 936,000 / 1.8 = 520,000, not 508,000; 508,000 only falls out of (936,000 − 20,000 safety margin) / 1.8, which is what sprint.md's '916,000 → 508,000' describes. The paragraph additionally attributes the whole 1.4–1.8× under-count to cheval's estimate, whereas D-3.10b says cheval's chars/3.5 heuristic is ≈1.4× and 1.8× is the cl100k probe filler.
findings.failure_mode: An operator sizing Bridgebuilder input for claude-opus-5-5 from the CHANGELOG gets either a stale 916,000 (1.8× over the real generated budget, guaranteeing truncation or provider rejection) or a formula that yields 520,000 instead of the generated 508,000.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 916,000 context line with the current generated value, and state the formula as it is computed: (bound − the 20,000 safety margin) / MEASURED_TO_ESTIMATE_SAFETY, ≈508,000 estimated tokens. Attribute 1.4× to cheval's estimate and 1.8× to the probe filler as D-3.10b does.

findings.cross_file_justification: SDD D-3.11 and the CHANGELOG (both in the diff) add a partial-record catalog write path that PRD FR-3.5, shown as context in the diff's prd.md hunk, still forbids.
findings.description: PRD FR-3.5 still reads 'writes the catalog only on a clean verified bound' and SDD D-3.8 says the same. This diff adds --write-partial-as-operator-set (D-3.11, CHANGELOG) and records that the live claude-opus-5-5 entry was written from a partial record (probe_outcome: partial, sample_size: 5). The diff edits FR-1.5 for exactly this kind of label drift but leaves FR-3.5 contradicting shipped behaviour and the live catalog state. sprint.md's MVP line likewise still says an unclean bound ends as '180K kept'.
findings.failure_mode: The acceptance spec says one thing and the catalog carries another. The next FR-3 review or guard test written from FR-3.5 will flag the live entry as a spec violation, and a downstream mount reading the PRD has no way to learn that a partial record can legitimately reach the catalog.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend FR-3.5 and SDD D-3.8 to: 'writes the catalog only on a clean verified bound, or on a partial record when the operator passes --write-partial-as-operator-set, in which case probe_outcome: partial is written to the entry'. Update the sprint.md MVP line to the same effect.

findings.cross_file_justification: The CHANGELOG effort bullet and SDD D-2.8 are both in the diff and describe the chain-walk effort rule differently.
findings.description: The CHANGELOG says 'A hop the chain walk reaches that declares no default inherits the effort resolved for the requested entry', which implies a per-hop rule where a hop that does declare params.default_effort or extra.effort uses its own value. SDD D-2.8 says effort 'is resolved once against the head entry and carried on the request to every hop' with no conditional. Under D-2.8, declaring default_effort: low on claude-headless has no effect when it is reached from opus; under the CHANGELOG reading it would win.
findings.failure_mode: An operator follows the CHANGELOG's advice to declare a default on the CLI entry expecting it to govern fallback hops, and the walk sends --effort high anyway (or, if the implementation matches the CHANGELOG, D-2.8's pin and finding-54 refutation are wrong).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'that declares no default' qualifier from the CHANGELOG and state D-2.8's rule plainly: effort is resolved once for the requested entry and carried to every hop; a CLI entry's own default applies only when that entry is the one requested.

findings.description: D-1.8 says 'Only a direct --model gemini-headless raises AgyOptInRequiredError' and that a gated hop in a chain is skipped and 'the walk continues to the next hop'. D-1.9 says any Google voice under effective cli-only routes to agy. The two leave two cases unspecified: (a) a direct --model gemini-2.5-pro under LOA_HEADLESS_MODE=cli-only, which routes to agy but is not the literal gemini-headless; (b) a chain whose every hop is gated (the stock Google chain under cli-only), where 'continue to the next hop' has nowhere to go. Neither doc says which error class terminates these walks.
findings.failure_mode: If the terminal error for an all-gated walk is the generic exhausted-chain class (PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE or similar) rather than INVALID_CONFIG/opt_in_required, FR-1.5's 'never trips a breaker' and 'not planned rather than failed' guarantees are violated for exactly the configuration (cli-only hosts) the opt-in is meant to protect, and the MODELINV envelope misreports the voice as failed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to D-1.8: a walk in which every hop is gated terminates with AgyOptInRequiredError (INVALID_CONFIG, failure_class opt_in_required, no breaker increment), and a direct Google voice under effective cli-only is treated as the direct gemini-headless case. Pin both with a test alongside the existing no-breaker-increment test.

findings.cross_file_justification: The CHANGELOG generalises a safeguard that SDD D-3.10b (in the diff) scopes to the Anthropic HTTP adapter only.
findings.description: The CHANGELOG states that 'on a calibrated entry cheval asks the provider's free count_tokens once the estimate passes half the bound and gates on the exact count'. D-3.10b scopes this to 'the Anthropic HTTP adapter's count_tokens trigger'. The calibration was taken on claude-headless, which is also this repo's primary route (KF-040: direct API unreachable), and the CLI has no count_tokens. On that route the only gate is cheval's chars/3.5 estimate, which under-counts by ≈1.4×, so prompts estimated between ≈670,000 and 936,000 pass the gate and are rejected by the CLI pre-flight.
findings.failure_mode: Operators on the headless route read the CHANGELOG and believe an exact-count gate protects them near the window; in practice such requests fail with PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT and are 'not walked', so the fallback chain is never tried for a request that a tighter estimate would have preempted or routed.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the CHANGELOG sentence: the exact-count gate applies on the HTTP transport only; on the claude-headless route cheval gates on its estimate and the CLI pre-flight is the backstop (no spend, PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT, not walked). Consider applying a 1/1.4 divisor to the headless pre-dispatch gate for calibrated entries, mirroring Bridgebuilder's MEASURED_TO_ESTIMATE_SAFETY.

findings.description: D-3.12 makes a persisting tokens-per-minute 429 a size step (failure_class: token_limit). D-3.11's write path checks only clean|partial. A bisection whose rejections are all TPM 429s on a rate-limited account therefore ends 'clean' and writes probed_ceiling / effective_input_ceiling with method: probed_headless into the shared catalog, which the CHANGELOG says downstream mounts inherit. An account quota is not a model context ceiling; the catalog already distinguishes the two via account_limits.
findings.failure_mode: A probe run on a TPM-limited account publishes an artificially low model ceiling to every mount; because 'a bound below the old one is written, never kept' and the observation store is tighten-only, the bound is not self-correcting on hosts with a higher tier.
findings.suggested_fix: Have write_catalog_operator_set() refuse (or require an explicit flag for) a record whose bounding rejection carries failure_class token_limit, and direct such outcomes to account_limits rather than probed_ceiling. Record the bounding failure_class in ceiling_calibration alongside probe_outcome.
